transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-22 08:15 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Ortega (Redwood SE), Rohit Desai (Redwood CSM); Sophie Blake (NexaCloud Alliances), Miles Tan (NexaCloud Partner AM), Aditi Rao (NexaCloud Technical Lead)

Summary (auto):  Align on co-sell sprint scope, nominate 8 accounts, pick 3 pilot plays, share pricing and technical constraints.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in, i'll kick off. is everyone good on audio?
[00:18] Sophie Blake: yep good here, thanks maya. excited to get this moving, q1 is heavy so want to lock priority accounts.
[01:05] Maya Chen: quick intro - we're planning a 4 week co-sell sprint, intent is to get two pilots live (one enterprise, one mid-market) and a third proof-of-value for an embed play. lucas will run the technical gating, rohit on success metrics.
[02:10] Lucas Ortega: hi all, just a heads up we need to validate the private deployment path for the enterprise pilot early - VPC peering and KMS for keys. if those aren't signed off it blows the timeline.
[03:45] Miles Tan: quick question, how strict is the VPC requirement? some of our customers prefer hosted but need data residency controls.
[04:20] Lucas Ortega: hosted (redwood api) can work for most but enterprise wants dedicated/priv setups. there is a tradeoff: hosted faster but less control, dedicated/private adds security but onboarding takes 2-4 weeks more.
[05:05] Sophie Blake: that's exactly the tradeoff we hit with EdgeServe last quarter, their dedicated setup was a blocker. need to know cost delta.
[06:35] Maya Chen: right, we'll share a delta sheet. it's roughly the batching/throughput sizing plus a platform fee for private. lucas can give rough numbers.
[07:10] Lucas Ortega: for the enterprise pilot i estimate if they need dedicated GPUs and VPC, add ~25-30% to per-token cost in our ballpark due to reserved capacity; hosted is lower but variable. i'll put numbers into a simple model.
[09:30] Aditi Rao: technical note: our connector expects a stable kv-cache and low-latency for retrieval use cases. what are your observed p95 latencies on the hosted api?
[10:05] Lucas Ortega: p95 depends on model and sequence len; for the family of smaller open models it's sub 200ms typical, for large-gen models it's 450-700ms in hosted. again, with dedicated pools we can get consistent p95 in the 150-250ms range.
[11:50] Miles Tan: ok, so for the mid-market pilot we can probably accept hosted, for enterprise we should plan for dedicated/private.
[14:00] Maya Chen: commercial — Sophie, can you run through priority accounts and ideal motion? who owns introductions?
[14:25] Sophie Blake: we have eight targets: OrbiBank (enterprise, compliance heavy), Datacore (mid-market), HelioMed (healthcare regulated), Clearview Retail, ArcFleet, SummitLogix, Greenline Energy, and Omega Insights. we can intro for OrbiBank, Datacore, HelioMed first three weeks.
[16:10] Rohit Desai: success criteria — for OrbiBank we want 5% reduction in manual review time and sub 300ms p95 for their workflow. pilot acceptance after 4 weeks of usage and a business impact report.
[17:05] Sophie Blake: timeline wise OrbiBank is tied to their procurement window end of jan, so we need a LOE to get to pilot by mid-jan.
[18:40] Maya Chen: action — we'll prioritize OrbiBank and Datacore as first two pilots. Sophie will send the prioritized list and expected ARR motion by friday.
[20:20] Aditi Rao: on infra gating, we'll need SAML SSO + SCIM and audit log retention for OrbiBank, they require 7 year logs i think — is that supported?
[21:05] Lucas Ortega: audit logs are supported, retention durations are configurable in our console retention tiers, but long-term archiving we'd need to discuss storage/price. SAML and SCIM we have integrations; we might need to validate attribute mappings.
[22:50] Miles Tan: also can you confirm certifications? OrbiBank will ask for SOC2 and ISO attestation documents.
[23:30] Maya Chen: yes we have SOC 2 type II and ISO 27001, and we'll share the security pack and pen-test summary link after this call.
[25:15] Sophie Blake: excellent, please add the compliance packet in the next email.
[26:00] Aditi Rao: minor transcription/clarify — when you said "KV cache" earlier, do you mean long lived persisted cache or ephemeral session cache? that affects connector design.
[27:00] Lucas Ortega: good catch — we mean prefix/KV that persists across sessions for retrieval augmentation, but not indefinite persistence, we can plug in customer vector store pointers. i'll document the semantics.
[28:15] Maya Chen: commercial ask — what's your expected discount rate for deals where Nexa is bringing introductions vs pure self-serve?
[29:05] Sophie Blake: typically we ask for 20-30% partner discount for introduced deals, smaller for co-sell where we share motion.
[30:40] Maya Chen: we have a partner pricing band, we'll propose an initial co-sell uplift and a pilot discount. i'll drop the paper.
[32:00] Miles Tan: competitor risk — both EdgeServe and VertexAI are quoting a one-click dedicated offer; how do we position?
[33:20] Lucas Ortega: differentiation is in predictable unit economics and tooling for rollouts, plus prefix caching and KV semantics. also our Optimize toolkit recommends batching/quantization to lower cost without sacrificing quality.
[34:00] Aditi Rao: for the OrbiBank data residency question, can Redwood provide a VPC-only private control plane so data never leaves their cloud?
[34:40] Lucas Ortega: yes, our Private mode supports customer-managed networking, can be scoped to VPC-only with customer KMS. onboarding time and infra footprint vary.
[36:10] Sophie Blake: will you run a joint benchmark with our infra team? we want numbers with their snapshot workloads.
[36:35] Lucas Ortega: yes we'll need sample tokens, prompt shapes, and sequence length distributions. Aditi can share the sample set.
[37:50] Aditi Rao: i'll send a small batch of redacted prompts and a workload profile. do you need data residency or just network access?
[38:20] Lucas Ortega: for bench we'd prefer a staging VPC with the same egress rules; if not, we can do a synthetic but it's less accurate.
[39:55] Maya Chen: on governance — we also need to map decision makers and procurement at OrbiBank. Sophie, can you introduce us to the procurement lead?
[40:30] Sophie Blake: yes i'll loop in Lina Park (procurement) and vendor-security lead. expect intro by tuesday.
[42:10] Rohit Desai: measurement — dashboard we provide will surface token spend by route, p95 by model, and a quality regression alert for top 20 prompts. we'll map to OrbiBank success metrics.
[43:45] Miles Tan: okay can you show us a sample of the dashboard? maybe in the pilot planning session.
[44:20] Maya Chen: we'll include a short console walkthrough in the pilot planning call.
[45:10] Sophie Blake: commercial mechanism — how do trials convert to ARR? do you provide trial credits, or partner-led PO?
[45:40] Maya Chen: usually pilot contract has a 30 day paid pilot with reduced price, credits are for early dev. we'll propose a 60% pilot discount for introduced proof-of-value and then standard rates on conversion.
[47:35] Aditi Rao: any red flags we should call out now?
[48:00] Lucas Ortega: potential risk is timeline — procurement windows in target accounts are tight; another is competing offers from big clouds who promise one-click dedicated endpoints.
[49:45] Sophie Blake: procurement timing noted. we'll prioritize intros that have January cycles.
[50:20] Maya Chen: recap: Maya send pricing and co-sell spreadsheet by friday (2026-12-24), Lucas to provide latency/cost models for three pilots by 2026-12-27, Aditi to share prompts and infra notes by 2026-12-28. Sophie to send prioritized list and init intros by 2026-12-24. schedule pilot planning session for 2026-12-29.
[51:30] Miles Tan: all good, thanks everyone.
[51:50] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in email with deck and links to security pack.
[52:00] Meeting ended.
